title: Implement a method to add a launcher to the panel via right-click
line: Add Widgets now offers a "Launcher Icon" widget that asks which application or command to launch when you add it.
explanation: The generic Icon widget, which launches a .desktop file, was marked NoDisplay, so the only ways to make a launcher were dragging an app from the menu or pinning a running window; an arbitrary program or command could not be added from the panel's right-click menu. The change lists the widget in Add Widgets as "Launcher Icon", and when it is added without a target it opens the standard Choose Application dialog; picking an app or typing a command (saved as a new .desktop file) sets the icon.

commits.message:
applets/icon: expose the widget in Add Widgets as "Launcher Icon"

The Icon widget was hidden, so there was no way to add a launcher for an
arbitrary program from the panel's own menus. It is now listed, and when
it is added without a target it asks which application or command to run.

BUG: 427550

Subject: [PATCH] applets/icon: expose the widget in Add Widgets as "Launcher
 Icon"

The Icon widget was hidden, so there was no way to add a launcher for an
arbitrary program from the panel's own menus. It is now listed, and when
it is added without a target it asks which application or command to run.

BUG: 427550

 #include <KDesktopFile>
@@ -26,6 +27,7 @@

 #include <KLocalizedString>
 #include <KNotificationJobUiDelegate>
+#include <KOpenWithDialog>
 #include <KProtocolManager>
 #include <KService>
 #include <KServiceAction>
@@ -60,6 +62,10 @@ IconApplet::~IconApplet()
 
 void IconApplet::init()
 {
+    m_popupTimer = new QTimer(this);
+    m_popupTimer->setSingleShot(true);
+    connect(m_popupTimer, &QTimer::timeout, this, &IconApplet::showConfigurationDialog);
+
     populate();
 }
 
@@ -68,6 +74,33 @@ void IconApplet::configChanged()
     populate();
 }
 
+void IconApplet::showConfigurationDialog()
+{
+    const QString entryName = u"url"_s;
+    KOpenWithDialog *openWithDialog = new KOpenWithDialog();
+    openWithDialog->setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose);
+    openWithDialog->setSaveNewApplications(true);
+
+    connect(openWithDialog, &QDialog::finished, this, [this, openWithDialog, entryName](int result) {
+        if (result != QDialog::Accepted) {
+            return;
+        }
+
+        const KService::Ptr service = openWithDialog->service();
+
+        Q_ASSERT(service);
+        if (!service || service->entryPath().isEmpty()) {
+            return; // Don't crash if KOpenWith wasn't able to create service.
+        }
+
+        m_url = QUrl::fromLocalFile(service->entryPath());
+        config().writeEntry(entryName, m_url);
+
+        populate();
+    });
+    openWithDialog->open();
+}
+
 void IconApplet::populate()
 {
     const QString entryName = u"url"_s;
@@ -84,15 +117,25 @@ void IconApplet::populate()
     const QString path = localPath();
     if (QFileInfo::exists(path)) {
         populateFromDesktopFile(path);
+        m_popupTimer->stop();
         return;
     }
 
     if (!m_url.isValid()) {
-        // invalid url, use dummy data
+        // We wait 100ms before displaying a dialog since
+        // when we create a valid icon applet (e.g. by drag
+        // and dropping an application from kickoff to the
+        // panel), the widget is first created and then
+        // the URL is immediately set. Without a timer, the
+        // dialog will be immediately created, even if
+        // the URL will be set immediately.
+        m_popupTimer->start(100);
         populateFromDesktopFile(QString());
         return;
     }
 
+    m_popupTimer->stop();
+
     const QString plasmaIconsFolderPath = QStandardPaths::writableLocation(QStandardPaths::GenericDataLocation) + QLatin1String("/plasma_icons");
     if (!QDir().mkpath(plasmaIconsFolderPath)) {
         setLaunchErrorMessage(i18n("Failed to create icon widgets folder '%1'", plasmaIconsFolderPath));

 };

media.caption: Add Widgets, search "launcher": no widget to launch a program of your choice
The new "Launcher Icon" widget is listed
Added to the panel, it opens Choose Application
After choosing System Settings, its icon sits in the panel
Clicking the icon launches System Settings
